title: The Gourmet Supremos: The Importance of Eating Well
description: Something seems to have Parvaneh of the Gourmet Supremos all in a fluster...

mainQuestExcel.title: The Gourmet Supremos: The Importance of Eating Well
mainQuestExcel.description: Something seems to have Parvaneh of the Gourmet Supremos all in a fluster...

dialogs.text: Parvaneh... and Traveler? What brings you here?
I came to help.
Really? Thank you so much! Now, Julie seems to have gone deeper within...
There are tons of monsters there. It's hard to deal with them with just the two of us. But we should be much better off with your help.
Let's get going. Julie should be in the woods.
I'm here for the big feast you promised.
No problem. But I can't cook it alone.
Traveler, could you do me a favor and help us get Julie back first?
Julie seems to have gone deeper in... and there are tons of monsters there. It will hard going with just the two of us.
After we find Julie, I'll make you the feast I promised.
Hey! If you break the wok, what will we cook with!?
Don't underestimate Liyue's skill in making woks. This is a unique cast iron wok specially designed for tossing. It won't break easily.
Besides, it's just a few monsters. What kind of iron wok would it be if it couldn't knock them flat?
You're expecting too much out of it...
Xudong has quite a bit of swagger.
Of course! A chef has to carry himself in a certain way.
I've never heard of such a thing! Why would a chef learn to smash monsters with an iron pot?!
Okay. Julie, let's get out of here. And fast...!
W—Wait! We have to help Uncle Munehisa! He's fighting against Kairagi in the woods, all alone.
Kairagi? Not monsters? How did you get involved with them?
I—I'll tell you later... Let's go help him! He's all alone...
Alright, I got it. Traveler, could you come with us?
Let's do this.
Come on, let's go!
You're going to fight the Kairagi?
Definitely. My wok's raring to go, see?
Besides, chefs can't run away on the eve of battle.
I told you not to have such high standards for chefs or their iron woks!
Where can I buy a wok like yours?
Haha, great question. I had it specially cast at Hanfeng's Ironmongers.
It's said to have materials excavated from the Chasm added to the iron. If you want to get one, go to Hanfeng's Ironmongers.
But I heard that the Chasm has been locked down for a long time. I doubt he would be able to make any now...
Parvaneh's handling herself just fine, too.
Huh? Well... hahaha, I just threw a few books at the monster's heads. You were the one who fought them off.
Wait. Where is "Along with Divinity Volume 6"? Did I throw it, too? I haven't finished that one yet!

flow.stepDescription: Look for traces of Kamei Munehisa up ahead

dialogs.text: Ahem... Sorry that you have to see me like this.
Uncle Munehisa, are you okay?...
Just a few lost go-arounds. No big deal.
Now, Julie, could you tell us the whole story, then?
Tell me everything please, or my books were wrecked for nothing... Agh, the pages are all wrinkled now...
It's simple... I just wanted to bring him some food.
*sigh*... You only met him once. Why... do you trust him so much?
I'm sure he's a good man! He was starving, but he gave the food to us instead of keeping it for himself.
Anyone who is willing to share food with others when they are hungry must be a good person!
Your concept of good and evil is so straightforward and pure...
You must live in some fairy tale world instead of Teyvat.
Hahaha, I think she's right, though.
I agree. Those who can uphold their honor and decency when they are hungry can't be all that bad.
Such simple and straightforward logic...
Anyway, Julie, do continue.
So I made some Chicken-Mushroom Skewers and wanted to try my luck finding him where we first met.
I did see him there, as it turned out.
I was just about to say hello when I noticed that he was confronting some Kairagi.
I wanted to get away, but I was spotted by them...
I'll take it from here...
Among those... people, are some of my old friends who served with me under the Shogunate.
After Inazuma's sudden change, we all left the Shogunate one after another to make our own living.
Is that how they make a living?
...Yes. We don't have any way to make money other than by the sword.
Since then, they became the Kairagi as you see them, making a living by plundering.
I didn't want to live like that, so I've wandered the land looking for work.
But no one would dare hire me as soon as they found out that I used to be a samurai who had left the Shogunate.
Since then, as you can see, I've had to scavenge for food in the wilderness.
Recently, my former comrades seem to be short-handed, so they have come every day to persuade me to join them. I refused every time.
Today... when Julie appeared, they thought that I must've joined some Clan or another and was trying to get rid of them. So they attacked us.
An unreasonable bunch...
They've never acted reasonably. But in their situation... there really isn't any reasoning to be done.
So he went to deal with those guys and I stayed where I was, waiting for him to return. Then suddenly, a group of monsters appeared...
You should have been able to deal with them, right?
Usually, I could. But I didn't eat anything when I left this morning, so I was too hungry. I didn't have any energy.
I lost all the Chicken-Mushroom Skewers on me when I was spotted by those Kairagi... Luckily I had Uncle Munehisa to protect me.
That's why breakfast is so important.
There are still many of these unreasonable Kairagi in Inazuma. We're going to be here for a while, and it just doesn't feel safe...
We can deal with a few weak monsters, but there's no way we can handle a group of people who know martial arts...
Uh... Uncle, you just mentioned that you're looking for a job, right?
How would you like to come with us?
Yay, that would be great!
But since he's a samurai who left the Shogunate, wouldn't he get us into trouble in Inazuma?
That's true. If I go with you, I might get you into trouble.
Hahaha, I don't think it matters. We're just going around looking for cooking ingredients.
The best thing a person in his situation can do is to stay far away from anything to do with the Shogunate or samurai.
If you work for someone as a guard or in a security detail, you're more likely to attract suspicion.
Plus, I don't think it would be right to let a good man like you starve.
I doubt I can fix anything else as a chef, but I can at least make sure that you're well-fed.
Sir, you...
Hehe. Well, what do you think? Would you like to join us? We can't offer much pay, but there will be plenty of food.
In that case, I am at your service, sir.
Woohoo!
This is a good thing, right? Yeah, this is for the best...
All right! I'm sure everyone is starving after all that work. This isn't a great place to cook... but I'll find a way to whip something up...
Traveler, have a rest. I'll take care of it. You just wait here.
Okay, time to get started!
Done... haha. Onigiri made of leftover rice. It's a bit rough... but it will fill your stomach. Come on, let's eat.
Traveler, thank you for coming with us. This recipe is for you. Uncle Munehisa just gave it to me, and I made you a copy.
He said it's a recipe he got while he was still working for the Shogunate. It's quite unique. You can give it a try if you're interested.
Alright then. Enough talk. Let's eat!
Well, guess you won't be skipping breakfast from now on.
A sensitive lot, huh.
It's not surprising, considering their position.
I think they were just using any excuse to deal with a "disobedient" person like me. To throw their weight around a bit.
After all, I have repeatedly refused them. It must have come as a blow.
Are all the Kairagi...
Not all. But regardless, they were all cowards who raise their swords against the weak.
Why did you leave the Shogunate?
I just... couldn't agree with what the Shogunate was doing in Inazuma.
I'm just a martial artist. I don't know what's good for the country or not.
I only knew that it went against what was in my heart, so I chose to leave.
Hehe. Perhaps I was just too old-fashioned... Please try not to laugh.
Ah, full at last... Hmm...
Why did you help him?
Do you mean Uncle Munehisa? I did it out of my professional ethics as a chef, of course.
Hah, just kidding. But I really don't want to see a good man like him go hungry.
In truth... I don't want to see anyone go hungry.
Hunger is a terrible feeling. I've had first-hand experience.
People can do terrible things under the influence of hunger.
I think that if everyone in this world ate well, perhaps, a lot of terrible things could be avoided.
I can't do it alone, true, but as a chef, I can at least try to help the people around me eat well.
Hahaha, to put it simply, I just want everyone to have food and eat well. A rather meaningless ideal, I suppose.
No, it's a noble ideal.
Hehe, thanks a lot. Okay... no more talking. Have some more and don't leave any on your plate. Wasting food is a terrible sin.
See you later.
You're leaving? Not having any seconds?
Hehe. This is actually quite tasty. I'll definitely go for another round...
Why did you want to bring him food?
Well... I just didn't want to see him go hungry.
The last time I saw him, he seemed sad. I thought it was probably because he didn't have enough to eat.
So I wanted to bring some food to him. He won't be so sad once he's full, I thought.
What made you trust him?
That's... an adventurer's intuition. I'm very good at telling the good guys from the bad guys.
Only good people give out food when they're hungry...
See you around.
Bye. I'll never miss breakfast again...
I can't believe those two...
You still don't seem to trust him, huh?
You mean Kamei Munehisa? Of course not... we've only met him a few times, how could I trust him so quickly?
...But while I don't trust Kamei Munehisa, I do trust Xudong's judgment.
You're from the Akademiya?
Sort of. I was originally doing field research for the Akademiya when I met Xudong in Liyue.
He was planning to travel around and study recipes, and the topic I was studying happened to be related to food. After we talked a few times, we decided to travel together.
We first went to Mondstadt where we were surrounded by a bunch of monsters. That's when Julie came, and she helped us chase them away.
When she heard that we were traveling around looking for different cuisine, she joined us.
She said she was planning to go adventuring, but I have the feeling that she just wanted to have some good food...
We'll be going to Sumeru next. I'm almost done with my research, so it's time for me to go back to Akademiya.
When we get to Sumeru, I'll make sure they get a taste of our local specialties...
Goodbye.
Okay, goodbye.
What is the matter?
Why did you agree to join Xudong?
Like Xudong said, if I want to have enough to eat... working for him is my best option at the moment.
Besides, Julie and Xudong are both of high moral character, and it will be an honor to travel with them.
Parvaneh... is a thoughtful person. It is understandable she would be wary of me.
Besides, she is merely a little suspicious of me as opposed to rejecting me outright, and that... that is enough for me.
Have you really been just wandering around?
Indeed. I would never lie. Since I left the Shogunate, I've been just wandering around.
I usually fill my stomach with wild fruits and, when I'm lucky, fresh game.
Occasionally, I also help people to fight off monsters or Kairagi, which gets me at least some payment.
Hehe... For someone like me who has no skills other than wielding a sword, job opportunities are a bit scarce.
Not to mention my background of leaving the Shogunate. People always associate me with the Kairagi, and that makes it even harder to find work.
I have no home or family to go to in Inazuma. Since I had nowhere to go, I just wandered.
Why did you leave the Shogunate?
I just... couldn't agree with what the Shogunate was doing in Inazuma.
I'm just a martial artist. I don't know what's good for the country or not.
I only knew that it went against what was in my heart, so I chose to leave.
Hehe. Perhaps I was just too old-fashioned... Please try not to laugh.
See you later.
Farewell.
